summary: Intermittent control-plane TLS auth failures for private deployment caused by NAT ephemeral port reuse
summary_detail: Customer on Dedicated tier reports intermittent 5xx and streaming disconnects from their private deployment. Failures correlate with spikes of control-plane mutual-TLS renegotiation attempts. Initial analysis suggests client's NAT gateway is reusing ephemeral ports for new connections while previous connections are still in TIME_WAIT causing the platform's control-plane to reject repeated client certificate renegotiations.
description:
Issue summary: FinEdge Capital's Dedicated private deployment is experiencing intermittent control-plane authentication failures (TLS) that manifest as 5xx errors for SDK calls and abrupt gRPC streaming resets. Impact: customer-facing features that rely on streaming generation degrade for short windows (typically 30-90s) multiple times per day. They are on a reserved deployment in us-east-1 behind their corporate NAT appliance.

Observed behavior:
- SDK client attempts streaming generation, connection succeeds initially but may be reset mid-stream with TLS alerts or TCP RST.
- Control-plane logs show 'tls: certificate verify failed' and 'unexpected client hello' around the same timestamps.
- Customer reports correlated firewall/NAT logs showing ephemeral port reuse for the same source IP within seconds.

Why this ticket: Customer needs a root cause and a mitigation path since retries cause visible user-facing errors and increased token usage.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Deploy a private package using latest agent (v2.4.1) in customer VPC. 2) From a single NATted host, open 50 concurrent streaming SDK sessions over a short period (burst). 3) Observe client-side gRPC resets and control-plane TLS negotiation failures in logs. 4) Compare with NAT appliance logs to see ephemeral port reuse when source port gets recycled quickly.
logs: 2026-03-12T09:12:03Z control-plane auth: tls: handshake failure (client 10.1.22.58:49152) - unexpected client hello
2026-03-12T09:12:03Z sdk-proxy: stream reset with error code 14 (UNAVAILABLE) token=acct-***
Customer NAT syslog: conntrack: DELETE src=54.240.12.7:49152 dst=34.210.5.8:443 state=TIME_WAIT
Customer NAT syslog: NEW src=54.240.12.7:49152 dst=34.210.5.8:443 - port reused 2s after prior close
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: rapid ephemeral port reuse at customer NAT causes TCP/TLS state mismatches on Redwood's edge leading to aborted TLS renegotiations when mutual TLS is enforced. Confirmed by correlating control-plane TLS alerts and customer NAT logs timestamps. Reproduced in lab by enabling short ephemeral port timeout and forcing port reuse. Not a cert chain mismatch (cert SAN OK) and not a model artifact fetch issue. Packet captures show client hello overlapping previous connection residuals leading to 'unexpected client hello'.
Additional findings: Customer's NAT device aggressive PAT timeout is 1s for TCP ephemeral ports. Rolling restarts of our control-plane proxies during certificate rotation amplify the issue because some clients initiate quick re-connections that hit the reuse window.
comments: Priya Kothari: Logged customer's NAT port reuse patterns and shared initial correlation with NAT syslogs.
Liam O'Connor: Spun up lab environment to reproduce - confirmed failure when PAT timeout < 5s. Captured pcap showing overlapping TCP sequence space.
Customer (FinEdge NetOps): We can increase NAT timeout but this is an appliance managed by another team; need short-term mitigation from Redwood side.
SRE (Maya Lin): Implementing guard in proxy to detect immediate re-use of same 4-tuple and treat as new session only after small suppression window. Will test for compatibility with TLS mTLS flow.
Eng (Diego Ruiz): Investigating whether we can prefer client IP preservation via X-Forwarded-For over reusing same TCP connection to reduce renegotiation frequency for high-burst clients.
Support (Priya): Requested customer's NAT device model/version and agreed on a coordinated maintenance window for NAT timeout increase.
resolution:
Workaround applied: SRE deployed a suppression heuristic on the edge proxy that rejects client connections that reuse the same source IP:port to destination within 3 seconds and triggers a fast-path retry using a different upstream worker. This reduced incident rate significantly. Long term: Eng to add a configuration knob to recommend and detect short NAT PAT timeouts and to surface guidance in private-deploy docs. Customer to coordinate with NetOps to increase PAT idle timeout to >= 30s for TCP ephemeral ports.
Rollout notes: heuristic deployed to 3 canaries on 2026-03-13, rolled to us-east fleet on 2026-03-14 03:00 UTC. Monitoring: added metric 'edge.tls.renegotiation_rejects' and dashboard tile; alert threshold set at 5/min to escalate to SRE.
follow_up_actions: ENG-PLAT: expose 'nat-pat-warning' in console when private deploy stats indicate <30s ephemeral timeouts
DOCS: update private deploy networking guide with NAT recommendations and detection steps
SRE: validate suppression heuristic won't interfere with legitimate re-connections during certificate rotation windows
customer_communication: 2026-03-12: Notified FinEdge of investigation and temporary mitigations. 2026-03-14: Shared suppression rollout and recommended NAT timeout change. Customer agreed to schedule NetOps window next week.
public_notes: No customer data was exfiltrated. Issue caused availability blips; resolved with combination of proxy heuristic and customer NAT timeout increase plan.
